service_notes.notes: This train to the Thai-Cambodian border is hauled by a diesel locomotive and has 3rd Class carriages with fans. Tickets can only be bought at the station up to two hours before departure. One carriage has room for full sized bicycles. There are two trains to the Thai-Cambodian border a day. The afternoon train is a diesel railcar (No. 279). Going the other way, the diesel railcar (No. 280) returns in the morning and this diesel locomotive train (No. 276) in the afternoon.

This train from the Thai-Cambodian border is hauled by a diesel locomotive and has 3rd Class carriages with fans. Tickets can only be bought at the station up to two hours before departure. One carriage has room for full sized bicycles. There are two trains from the Thai-Cambodian border a day. No. 280 departs in the morning and this one in the afternoon. The outbound journey from Bangkok for this train is done by No. 275.

This train from the Thai-Cambodian is a diesel railcar and has 3rd Class carriages with fans. There is no room for full sized bicycles. You need to take the No. 276 train for this. Tickets can only be bought at the station up to two hours before departure. The return journey to Ban Klong Luk Border is done in the afternoon by No. 279 train.

notes: Overnight Rapid service with mixed seating and sleeping cars. It runs from Bangkok (Krung Thep Aphiwat) to Vientiane (Khamsavath) in Laos. Thai immigration is done at Nong Khai Station and Laos immigration at Vientiane (Khamsavath) Station. The train has 2nd and 3rd Class seats with fans, 2nd Class seats with air-conditioning, and 2nd class sleeper carriages. Advance booking is recommended as there are only two sleeper carriages. Your alternative is to take Special Express No. 25 and then switch to this train in Nong Khai to cross the border.

Overnight Rapid service with mixed seating and sleeping cars. It runs from Vientiane (Khamsavath) in Laos to Bangkok (Krung Thep Aphiwat). Laos immigration is done at Vientiane (Khamsavath) Station and Thai immigration at Nong Khai Station. The train has 2nd and 3rd Class seats with fans, 2nd Class seats with air-conditioning, and 2nd class sleeper carriages. Advance booking is recommended as there are only two sleeper carriages. Your alternative is to take this train to Nong Khai and then switch to Special Express No. 26 to go to Bangkok. Make sure you let officials know you are taking the earlier train and they will let you go to the front of the immigration queue. Timetable updated on 1st February 2026.
